relatedSnapshot.title: Cold email daily sending limit under-allocated when a leadless completed campaign remains in the split
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The cold email daily sending limit is being under-allocated because the even-split logic counts finished campaigns that have no leads, cutting active campaigns' daily capacity by roughly 25%.

## Problem

A customer with 18 active inboxes and 3 active campaigns sends ~470 emails/day instead of ~630 because a fourth, completed campaign (with zero leads) is still counted as active in the split, diluting the daily-limit allocation.

## Root cause

`buildEvenSplitPlan` in `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/util.ts` divides total daily capacity (unique inboxes × 35) evenly across every campaign the provider reports as active with a non-empty email list, without excluding campaigns that have no leads. A completed campaign left "active" on the provider (Acquisity-side status desync) is counted, so 18×35=630 splits 4 ways (157 each) instead of 3 ways (210 each).

## Blast radius

622 organizations hold 1,556 leadless "completed" campaigns that are still display-active with a non-empty email list. Counted 2026-09-04: `status = 'completed' AND display_status = 'active' AND total_leads = 0 AND jsonb_array_length(settings->'emailAccounts') > 0`. Confirmed affected: 1 organization (this report); potentially exposed: 622 organizations.

## Proposed fix

Exclude campaigns with no leads (or campaigns Acquisity has marked completed/paused) from the daily-limit even split so capacity is divided only across campaigns that can actually send, and deactivate completed campaigns on the provider so they leave the active list.

## What's included

Fix the split to exclude leadless/completed campaigns; containment is deactivating the ghost campaigns for affected orgs; observability is a signal for leadless campaigns present in the split.

## Regression seam

`buildEvenSplitPlan(campaigns, inboxes)`: given 18 inboxes, 3 campaigns with leads, and 1 leadless campaign, it must return 210/day for each of the 3 real campaigns (not 157) and emit no plan entry for the leadless campaign.

## Done when

* The split excludes leadless/completed campaigns.
* A regression test proves 18 inboxes + 3 leaded campaigns + 1 leadless campaign yields 210 (not 157) per leaded campaign.
* Affected organizations are rebalanced to their full capacity.

## Reports

* ENG-13501

relatedSnapshot.title: One-off recovery: backfill + AI SDR replay for the webhook-outage cohort (99 + 207)
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Reopened 2026-06-23 per James (Slack P0 thread) — this is the live one-off recovery run for the webhook-outage cohort.** Previous cancellation reversed so the resync → backfill → AI-SDR-replay is tracked on record (not just in-flight Slack work).

## Problem

During the silent webhook outages, prospect replies arrived while webhooks were down. We've resynced + backfilled most affected workspaces but have NOT re-run AI SDR on those imported replies — importing does not trigger AI SDR (verified in code) — so prospects sit un-answered. Several clients have had this for a couple of weeks and think their campaigns aren't working.

Cohorts: 99 (May-20) resynced+backfilled, not replayed; 207 active-campaign silent dropouts (158 resynced+backfilled, ~49 pending resync, none replayed); plus the two named system-provisioned workspaces `<workspace-slug>` and `<workspace-slug>` (whose admin "resync" never actually re-registered — confirmed via Inngest: no resync run fired).

## Plan (one-off scripts; reuse existing primitives; no new app code)

Strictly ordered, with wait points (ordering is load-bearing):

0. **Detect** — read-only script: active Company Two provider + ≥1 active campaign + 0 `outreach_webhook_event` in last N days → org-id list. Confirm count ≈ cohort and that the two named workspaces appear.
1. **Re-register** — fire `OUTREACH_EVENTS.RESYNC_WEBHOOKS` per org (batched; `processResyncWebhook` caps concurrency at 5; uses the shipped create-then-swap from PR #4945). Wait for completion.
2. **Backfill (windowed)** — `OUTREACH_EVENTS.EMAIL_THREADS_BULK_IMPORT` `{ organizationIds, userId: <superadmin>, classifyInterest: true }`. Wait for completion.
3. **Replay** — select positive / last-from-prospect / non-human-owned / non-terminal threads → `admin.sdrReplay.replayThreads` in ≤300-id batches (re-verifies prospect-sent-last before firing).

Depends on PR #4945 (the safe-resync prerequisite). Every driver script ships with a `--dry-run`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All affected orgs (99 + 207 + the 2 named) re-registered and confirmed delivering.
- [ ] Missed messages backfilled (windowed to the silent period; no full-history walk).
- [ ] AI SDR replayed on unanswered prospect threads; no double-replies (idempotency/guards respected).
- [ ] Never replays human-owned (`controlLevel` in human_takeover/dnc/paused/escalated) or terminal-lifecycle (booked/completed/declined) threads.
- [ ] Per-phase structured summary (orgs resynced, threads imported, replays fired/skipped/failed).

Name 4 this flow (auto on every future reconnect) → ENG-10710. Detection / zombie webhooks → ENG-10661 + ENG-10711.

relatedSnapshot.title: Cold Email Agent campaign volume not reallocating after pauses
relatedSnapshot.description:
Customer reports that the Cold Email Agent campaign "Medical & Dental Groups" is only sending \~88 emails per day across 15 inboxes.

Key context:

* Other campaigns were paused to concentrate volume on the Medical & Dental Groups campaign.
* Despite pausing other campaigns, daily volume has not increased and remains around 5–6 emails per inbox per day (\~88/day total).
* On January 1st, the system sent around 450 emails in a single day; since then, volume has dropped and stabilized at \~88/day.
* Inboxes have been warming for about 4 weeks, so current volume is lower than expected for this stage.
* Support review suggests this may be a send-cap allocation or throttling issue where volume does not reallocate correctly after campaigns are paused.

There is a Jam screen recording linked in the conversation showing the current setup and behavior.

Please investigate why sending volume is not scaling back up on the remaining active campaign after other campaigns are paused and whether the campaign is stuck in an incorrect reduced send cap state.

relatedSnapshot.title: Investigate email send volume and campaign issues for client
relatedSnapshot.description:
User problem summary:

The issues reported are:

* The campaign is expected to send 225 new emails per day across 15 email accounts, but only 195 emails per day are being sent, leaving a discrepancy of about 30 emails per day.
* The campaign appears to have stopped sending Step 1 emails after May 6th, despite there being 14,000 leads loaded and the expectation that new leads should continue entering the sequence daily.
* The client configured a 7-step sequence with multiple variants and 2–3 day gaps, but wants every lead to receive all 7 steps sequentially regardless of whether they respond.
* The client needs confirmation on whether the platform supports this type of sequential sending behavior and whether the current setup could be affecting performance.
* The same slow campaign performance issue reportedly happened in a previous campaign, raising concerns about a recurring account-level or platform-level issue.
* The client is requesting:
  * investigation into the missing send volume,
  * explanation and resolution for the campaign stopping after May 6th,
  * clarification on sequence behavior/support,
  * review of historical account issues,
  * and guidance on whether reducing sequence complexity would improve performance.

#### Customer Name

Name 8

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 8

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Support Ticket: Campaign Performance Issues Client Overview: The client has 5 domains with 3 email accounts per domain totalling 15 email accounts. He has 14,000 leads loaded into the campaign and all 15 email accounts have been confirmed as added to the campaign. Expected vs Actual Send Volume: With 15 email accounts sending 15 new emails per day the expected daily send volume is 225 new emails per day. Between May 5th and May 6th the expected total should have been 450 new emails across two days. However only 195 emails per day are going out which means approximately 30 emails per day are unaccounted for. We need to understand why the actual send volume is falling short of the expected volume despite all 15 accounts being active and added to the campaign. Campaign Stopped Sending After May 6th: The campaign appears to have stopped sending emails to the first sequence after May 6th. We need to understand why this happened. Even accounting for a two to three day wait period between Step 1 and Step 2 the campaign should have continued sending Step 1 emails to new leads every single day without interruption. This needs to be investigated and resolved immediately. Sequence Structure Issue: The client has set up 7 steps with multiple variants per step and a two to three day gap between each step. It is important to note that in the interview method sequences are not designed to follow up with the same lead sequentially through all 7 steps. Each step should only trigger for leads that have not yet responded. However this client wants all 7 steps to go to every single lead in sequential form regardless of whether they have responded or not. We need confirmation on whether the platform supports this configuration and if so whether this setup could be contributing to the slower than expected send volume and the campaign stopping after May 6th. Historical Pattern: This is not the first time this client has experienced slow campaign performance. The same issue occurred with a previous campaign. This suggests there may be a deeper configuration issue or platform level problem specific to this client's account that needs to be reviewed comprehensively rather than just addressing the immediate symptoms. What We Need From Support:  Investigate why only 195 emails per day are going out instead of the expected 225 and identify the 30 email per day discrepancy. Explain why the campaign stopped sending after May 6th and resolve it immediately. Confirm whether the platform supports sending all 7 sequential steps to every lead regardless of response and advise on whether this configuration is causing performance issues. Review the client's account history given this has happened on a previous campaign and determine whether there is a recurring platform level issue. Advise on whether reducing the number of sequence steps would improve send volume and campaign performance and if so what the optimal configuration would look like.  Please prioritize this ticket as the client has 14,000 leads loaded and the campaign running at reduced capacity is significantly impacting their outreach volume and results. Thank you.

relatedSnapshot.title: [Docs gap] New campaigns ramp up sending gradually — no doc explains expected early volume
relatedSnapshot.description:
DOCS GAP: The Help Center explains inbox warmup thoroughly and mentions the hard cap of "30 campaign emails per inbox per day," but nothing explains that a newly launched campaign ramps up its daily send volume gradually over the first days/weeks — even when every attached inbox is fully warmed (green flame, Active). Customers (and CS) expect (#inboxes x ~30) = daily volume immediately and read the slow initial days as a bug. The docs cover inbox readiness but not campaign-level send ramp.

CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Name 10 (Company Eleven) launched a new campaign and reported only 54 emails sent in 2 days across 9 warmed/active inboxes, asking "it is going too slow, what is the problem?" Investigation shows this is expected ramp-up, not a defect (evidence below).

EVIDENCE (expected behavior, not a bug):

* Campaign "Company Twelve - 200 leads Healthcare Trial" (id <uuid>) was activated 2026-07-13.
* Daily emails_sent: 2026-07-13 = 18, 2026-07-14 = 36 (= 54 total, exactly matching the customer's report). Volume increasing day-over-day (~doubling) — a healthy ramp, not a stall.
* 9 attached inboxes all active + connected, mailbox_type = dfy, created 2026-06-25 (~3 weeks old, recently through initial warmup).
* Plenty of leads remain: 1,155 not_yet_contacted (1,209 total) — NOT lead-limited.
* outreach_provider is_active = true, no connection_error.
* Same org's mature campaign "Real Estate | Leadership | US | Name 11" (older March inboxes) sends ~260-270/day fine — confirms the platform sends at volume once ramped; the difference is the new campaign + newer inboxes.

SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add a short section (e.g. in your-first-campaign.mdx "What to check in the first 24 hours", or a new "How fast will my campaign send?" FAQ under cold-email-agent) explaining: (1) new campaigns start low and ramp up over the first ~1-2 weeks to protect deliverability; (2) newer domains/inboxes ramp more conservatively; (3) the per-inbox ceiling is ~30/day, so full volume ~= #inboxes x ~30 only once fully ramped; (4) low volume in the first couple of days with a small increasing trend is expected, not a fault.

RELATED DOC(S):

* apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/getting-started/your-first-campaign.mdx
* apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/email-accounts/warmup.mdx (covers inbox warmup, not campaign ramp)
* apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/email-accounts/health-and-troubleshooting.mdx
